name: Fabrika Centre for Creative Industries
funding: Self-funded: income of the Oktyabr technical-paper mill and rent of studios, under owner-director Asya Filippova; no major outside investors.
watch: Artist-in-residence programme for foreign artists suspended; Filippova says Fabrika has always lived on self-sufficiency with the owner's support.
records_note: This private creative cluster's site posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; it describes tenants, studios and programmes only.

name: Moscow International Biennale of Contemporary Art
funding: Private biennale foundation (Yulia Muzykantskaya); sponsor roster not published; 2022 edition hosted by the state Tretyakov Gallery.
watch: The 9th edition, due to open at the New Tretyakov on 7 Nov 2022, was cancelled on 3 Nov 2022 by the Ministry of Culture citing 'absolute mismatch' of exhibits with a federal museum and 'controversial content'. No edition since.
records_note: Its old website no longer loads and an archived copy is a hijacked gambling page, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked.

name: Moscow Museum of Modern Art (MMOMA)
funding: Moscow city (GBUK under the Department of Culture of Moscow); founded 1999 by Zurab Tsereteli (died Apr 2025), run by his grandson Vasili Tsereteli. Individual and corporate patron programme exists.
records_note: Posts a 2025 results report and balance sheets for 2015 to 2025, but names no sponsors or board; only management is listed.

name: Museum of Russian Impressionism
funding: Private: founded by Boris Mints (O1 Group) in 2016; since Feb 2024 the patron-trustee is Vladimir Voronin, shareholder of property developer FSK Group (property money, allowed).
watch: Mints left Russia and could no longer support the museum; Voronin began funding exhibitions in 2023 and took over as permanent trustee on 15 Feb 2024. OpenSanctions lists Mints only in an oligarch/Wikidata database, not on any sanctions list.
records_note: The museum's own site would not load from here, so its reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked; only press coverage was readable.

name: Singapore Art Museum
funding: FY23/24: state (Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth) plus Mapletree, Singapore Tourism Board, CHARLES & KEITH Foundation, New Carlsberg Foundation (alcohol).
watch: Board member Pierre Lorinet is a director of oil trader Trafigura (joined 1 Jul 2024). Roster is from FY23/24; the FY24/25 report was not found.
records_note: Its About page posts audited annual reports for FY2015 to FY2025, a named board, and the FY2025 report lists donors and sponsors.

name: Busan Museum of Art
funding: Municipal museum run by Busan Metropolitan City, reopened in 2026 after a 46.9bn-won rebuild; patrons' society members include BNK Busan Bank and Hwaseung Group.
watch: Curatorial dispute, Sept 2026: Korea Economic Daily called its reopening exhibition on defector and socialist-affiliated artists one-sided.
records_note: One undated page names patrons' society members such as BNK Busan Bank and Hwaseung Group; it posts no reports, accounts or board.

name: Busan Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Municipal museum on Eulsukdo, run by Busan Metropolitan City; it hosted part of the 2026 Busan Biennale.
watch: Museum site (busan.go.kr/moca) refused connections and has no Wayback snapshot, so the roster is unread. Only the building and garden have drawn criticism.
records_note: The museum site has no annual reports, accounts, sponsor list or board; it only shows an organisation chart and the governing ordinance.

name: CA2M Centro de Arte Dos de Mayo
funding: Funded by the Comunidad de Madrid.
records_note: Its transparency page holds only a 2024 organigram and budget; it posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: Bonniers Konsthall
records_note: No records of its own; parent Bonnier posts annual reviews 2015 to 2025, accounts 2016 to 2025 and its board; the konsthall lists no funders.

name: Taipei Contemporary Art Center
funding: Artist-run space founded 2010. In 2013 its director said most money came from sales of donated artworks, plus a small government subsidy (about 15%). No current funder list found.
watch: JUT Land Development gave the building 2009 to 2012. The centre's own site fails its certificate check; no 2025 or 2026 programme found.
records_note: Its website returns only an error page (live and in an August 2026 archive copy), so nothing could be checked.

name: Museo de Arte de El Salvador (MARTE)
watch: Sponsor wall lists Avanza Consultores, The Zemurray Foundation, C. Imberton, Alas Doradas, Viva Outdoor, AR and Ternova.
records_note: No annual reports or accounts found; six sponsor logos with no names are shown undated, and the board list names only its president.

name: Centro de Arte Fundación Ortiz-Gurdián
funding: Private family foundation (founded 1996, León museum opened 2000) paid for by founders Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga and Patricia Gurdián, Banpro and Grupo Promerica.
watch: Banking money (Banpro/Promerica, not under campaign). Ortega regime arrested Banpro's general manager in June 2021.
records_note: No reports or accounts found; no funder list beyond Banpro's credit on the Managua centre; the family board is named on the home page.
